findings.quote: The soap film has two free surfaces, so the work done equals the surface tension times twice the increase in the film's area.
findings.note: The question states a film of water, not a soap film, and gives the surface tension of water (0.07 N m⁻¹). The physics is unchanged, but naming the wrong liquid in the opening line can suggest the two-surface count applies only to soap films.
findings.fix: The water film has two free surfaces, so the work done equals the surface tension times twice the increase in the film's area.

notes: Independent solve: ΔA per face = 0.08 × (0.008 − 0.006) = 1.6×10⁻⁴ m²; W = T × 2ΔA = 0.07 × 3.2×10⁻⁴ = 2.24×10⁻⁵ J = 22.4 μJ, matching option 1. Both mistake entries were checked: one surface gives 11.2 μJ (option 4) and a factor 4 gives 44.8 μJ (option 3). The concept_tags also carry "soap film" for the same reason, but the tags are not reader-facing so I filed only the approach.
